header.name: Computational Methods in Oncology Research (CMOR)
header.description: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) target a one-third reduction in non-communicable disease (NCD) mortality between 2015-2030. Cancer accounts for 22% of NCD deaths. Worldwide, an estimated 19.3 million new cancer cases and almost 10.0 million cancer deaths occurred in 2020, making it one of the worst challenges against humanity. The advent of high-throughput omic platforms has opened many doors for substantial interventions in terms of cancer detection, prevention, treatment, and life expectancy analysis. This course is timely, practical and will prepare students as computational warriors against this curse.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to critique and write about molecular phenomena related to cancer

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to generate upstream and downstream processing pipelines for omic data in relation to cancer

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to design univariate, and multivariate analyses strategies to interrogate cancer samples

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to bring AI to bear in formulating and solving problems arising from the field of cancer detection and treatment

lecture_topics: Familiarity with major bioinofrmatic resrouces in cancer research
Processing of omic data in cancer
Prediction frameworks for cancer stage, type
Application I: Detection of cancer from blood leveraging AI
Application II: Tumour micro-environment deconvolution and immune infiltration analysis
Application III: Personalised medicine based on transcriptomics leveraging AI
Invited lectures: Target discovery, homology modeling, virtual screening and molecular dynamics in cancer drug discovery
